subject: Short brief: data pathways & subprocessors for Console / Hosted API
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Levy <sara@acmecorp.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Short brief: data pathways & subprocessors for Console / Hosted API

Hi Sara and team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great conversation. Procurement asked for a concise, "sales-friendly" one-pager that explains where customer data flows (hosted API + Console), who our subprocessors are for hosted control plane and telemetry, and what transfer safeguards we rely on for cross-border requests. They want it in plain language they can attach to the SOW.

Can we share a short (one page) set of bullet points and a single-line data flow diagram? Ideally:
- Two bullets on what data is processed by the hosted API vs what stays in the customer's Console (customer-configured logs, KV).
- One short line on subprocessors (top 5 names + roles) and where to find the full list.
- One short note on transfers and standard safeguards (SCCs, encryption in transit + at rest).

Procurement also attached their checklist and would like an estimate for how long legal will need to review the one-pager.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — can you take a first pass? I put Laura and Ben on cc because they'll own the sales copy + legal check.

Thanks,
Maya

--
Maya Srinivasan
Director, Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
maya_srinivasan@redwood.com
[Attachment: none]

Thanks, Maya — this is helpful. Procurement attached their checklist (see attached). A few clarifying asks from their side:
- Can you provide a single-line summary we can drop under "Data Handling" in the SOW?
- For subprocessors, they want names and short parenthetical roles (e.g., "Cloud infra (GCP), Observability (Honeycomb)").
- If possible, a one-sentence callout on whether customer prompt data is ever used for model training or internal metrics.

Procurement asked whether you have a DocuSign-ready DPA or if legal will need 5–7 business days to review a lightweight one-pager + DPA.

Attaching ProcurementChecklist.xlsx to show the exact fields they need.

Best,
Sara

sara@acmecorp.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft one-pager and shortlines for Acme procurement (internal)

Maya — first pass attached. I focused on plain language; Ben, can you run legal/litmus on the training line? Quick summary below that I think fits Procurement's checklist:

Console vs Hosted API (two-line bullets):
- Hosted API: We process prompts and return generated text. Prompt text is handled by the hosted runtime and temporary artifacts (like KV cache) are purged per customer settings; persistent logs (request/response traces) can be retained for X days for billing/operations.
- Console: The Console stores account settings, user management info, and optional export logs that customers control. Customers can enable/disable telemetry exports; when enabled, logs are sent to our observability subsystem and are subject to the retention window.

Subprocessors (top-level, single-line with roles):
- Google Cloud (GCP) — infrastructure (compute, storage)
- AWS S3 (for optional object storage exports) — storage
- Honeycomb — observability and tracing
- Sentry — error telemetry aggregation
- Fastly — CDN and edge delivery
(Full list and countries: link in footer)

Transfers and safeguards:
- Data in transit is encrypted (TLS); at rest encryption is used for customer data stores. For cross-border transfers we rely on EU SCCs where applicable and contractual safeguards; details in DPA.

Training and model usage callout (one sentence, draft):
- We do not use customer prompt data to train our base models; customers may opt in to sharing aggregated usage signals for model improvement under an explicit agreement.

Attached: console-privacy-onepager-draft.docx and a plain-text list console-transfer-bulletpoints-v2.txt.

Ben — if you confirm the training sentence is safe, I can push this to the shared Drive and produce a DocuSign-ready DPA link. Suggest keeping the one-pager at ~250 words.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Product Marketing | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
[Attachment: console-privacy-onepager-draft.docx (docx)]
[Attachment: console-transfer-bulletpoints-v2.txt (text)]

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Short brief: data pathways & subprocessors for Console / Hosted API

Sara — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a trimmed version (one-pager) and a one-line "Data Handling" sentence for the SOW. Laura and Ben have signed off on the training language below. I also included a link to the full subprocessor list and a DocuSign link for the DPA template if procurement wants to proceed.

One-line for SOW (drop-in):
"Redwood Inference processes customer requests on our hosted runtime; account settings and optional export logs are stored in the customer Console. We encrypt data in transit and at rest, and use standard contractual safeguards (EU SCCs) for cross-border transfers. See our public subprocessor list for details."

Training sentence (approved):
"We do not use customer prompt or file content to train our base models. Customers may opt in to share aggregated, anonymized usage signals for model improvement under explicit agreement."

Next steps:
- If procurement is happy, they can sign the DPA via the DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/link/Acme-Console-DPA
- If they need the full subprocessor map exported, I'll have legal export the CSV and drop it in Drive by EOD Monday.

Attachments: console-privacy-onepager-draft.docx (trimmed), console-transfer-bulletpoints-v2.txt.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if procurement wants to walk through the one-pager line-by-line.

Best,
Maya
